content.comment_body: Hello, I need assistance. I'm looking for a program example that records the time when an input is triggered and stores this information so it can be shown on the [product_name] display.

You can use the "Acknowledge message" function in the message text. This will display your message until you confirm it with the OK button on the [product_name], provided the error condition no longer exists.

Good evening, that program was useful, but I need to create a history that tracks the last three activation times of the input. When there is a fourth activation, it should overwrite the oldest record. I'd appreciate any help.

With [product_name], you cannot directly access or store the current time parameters. To achieve this, you would need to implement an auxiliary clock with its limits or retrieve time values from another device (for example, another [product_name]). There is an existing discussion about this in the German forum section. Once you have these time values, you would write them to a custom memory structure when triggered. The values from individual memory cells can then be displayed in the text display. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users intend to create a record of input trigger times and display this information on [product_name], but encounter notable restrictions. While simple acknowledgements can be shown, recording and maintaining histories of time-stamped events is limited because the platform does not support direct access to the system clock or robust memory management. Users are exploring alternative solutions as no straightforward method is available.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to be able to log and display multiple time-stamped input events in a rolling log format directly on the [product_name] device, allowing for easy review of recent activity.
